# Sirach Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_009_page_001.jpg

---

9:1 Do not be jealous of the wife of your bosom, lest you teach her a wicked lesson against yourself.

9:2 Do not give a woman power over your soul, lest she trample your strength.

9:3 Do not go to meet a strange woman, lest you fall into her snares.

9:4 Do not associate with a singing woman, lest you be caught by her wiles.

9:5 Do not gaze at a virgin, lest you stumble and incur penalties for her.

9:6 Do not give your soul to harlots, lest you lose your inheritance.

9:7 Do not look around in the streets of a city, nor roam the deserted parts of it.

9:8 Turn away your eye from a shapely woman, and do not gaze at beauty belonging to another; many have been seduced by a woman's beauty, and with it passion is kindled like a fire.

9:9 Never recline beside a married woman, nor drink the wine of revelry with her, lest your heart turn aside to her and in blood you slide down to destruction.

9:10 Do not abandon an old friend, for a new one does not compare with him; a new friend is like new wine — when it has aged you will drink it with pleasure.

9:11 Do not envy the success of a sinner, for you do not know what his end will be.

9:12 Do not delight in what pleases the ungodly; remember that they will not go unpunished to their grave.

9:13 Keep far from a man who has the power of killing, and you will not be haunted by the fear of death; but if you approach him, do not offend him, lest he take your life; know that you are treading among snares and are walking over a net.

9:14 As best you can, make an estimate of your neighbors, and take counsel with the wise.

9:15 Let your conversation be with men of understanding, and let all your discussion be about the law of the Most High.

9:16 Let righteous men be your dinner companions, and let your glory be in the fear of the Lord.

9:17 A work is praised for the skill of the craftsman, and a community leader is proved wise by his words.

9:18 A talkative person is dangerous in his city, and one who is reckless in speech will be hated.

---

*Translator's Note: The first half of this chapter (vv.1-9) treats relations with women and reflects Ben Sira's conventional patriarchal perspective — these warnings are directed at a male reader and are culturally specific to his time. Hebrew (Cairo Genizah MS A) is partially extant. vv.10-18 shift to choosing friends and rulers wisely. v.10 contains the beautiful simile of the old friend as aged wine.*
